subject: Mid-cycle course correction: scope reductions, blockers, and QBR artifacts
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Mid-cycle course correction: scope reductions, blockers, and QBR artifacts

Team —

Quick mid-cycle note ahead of next week’s QBR prep. We ran the OKR health check yesterday and the signal is clear: two objectives are tracking below expected velocity and will require scope tradeoffs and a short list of unblock actions to preserve customer-facing commitments. High level: 

- O1 (Reduce generation tail latency 95th): on-track for infra changes but we’re ~3 weeks behind on benchmark validation.
- O2 (Embedding throughput for similarity search): prototype done but not integrated with routing layer; integration slips will reduce throughput targets.
- O3 (Expand Redstone partner integration): legal/procurement gating is the critical path.

Asks / proposals:
1) Short scope carve: defer non-user-visible telemetry enhancements in O2 (estimate savings: 2 FTE-weeks) so eng can shift to routing integration.
2) SLA exception request for Acme pilot to allow temporary cross-region routing to hit latency SLOs while we finish residency config. Vanessa — can you sign off on a 6-week exception window? I attached sla-exception-request.pdf.
3) Procurement & legal: Marissa, can you accelerate the PO/DS schedule? Jenna from Acme is on copy; we need a mutual action plan + DocuSign path.
4) Infra ownership: Mateo to prioritize kernel selection & benchmark runs; aim for candidate build by Nov 19.
5) Security validation: Aditya, we need a small focused review for the routing fallback behaviour (not full pen-test) — target Nov 12.

Attachments: qbr_readout_v2.pptx (WIP deck), sla-exception-request.pdf (form), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (template). Drive folder link in metadata.

Goal for this thread: agree on who owns what and confirm updated milestones by Monday EOD so the QBR pack can reflect realistic asks and risks.

Thanks —
Priyom
Priyom Das
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle course correction: scope reductions, blockers, and QBR artifacts

Priyom —

Thanks for the concise callout. I agree with the carve for non-user telemetry in O2 — that’s low ROI for right now. A couple of operational notes:

- Mateo: please publish the benchmark plan by EOD Wednesday (what sequences, model variants, quantization profile).
- Vanessa: if we approve a 6-week SLA exception we should tie it to two conditions: (1) a clear rollback trigger and (2) weekly latency reports shared to the exec QBR channel.

I can adjust the QBR deck to show a mitigated risk lane vs. a hard miss, which will buy more runway for the eng fix. I’ll slot a 15-min readout in Wed’s leadership sync to align.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Strategy | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle course correction: scope reductions, blockers, and QBR artifacts

Looping in a short exec POV. I support the 6-week SLA exception for the Acme pilot on a conditional basis. Conditions I need for sign-off:

- A rollback trigger (latency > 1.8x baseline for two consecutive measurement windows).
- Weekly latency transparency (slice by region + model variant) sent to me and Laura.
- A security review note (Aditya) confirming no PII routing during the exception window.

Operational ask: if we reassign 1 engineer from the telemetry team to routing, what impact do we expect on the telemetry backlog? Laura — please quantify and add to the readout.

I’ve attached a light note (sla-exception-request.pdf) with the exception window language I’d like in the QBR appendix.

V
Vanessa Ortiz
Chief Operating Officer | Redwood Inference

Hi Priyom / Marissa —

Thanks for the transparency. From Acme’s side: we can accept a temporary routing exception as long as the following are true on our side:

- We get weekly latency reports (slice by region + model) and a single point-of-contact for incidents.
- Legal will need a simple addendum that covers the exception window and the rollback trigger.
- Procurement: we need the PO and initial invoice schedule to be set before we start pilot runs.

Procurement (cc’ed) — can you confirm earliest PO timeline? Also, does Redwood support the region restriction waiver for the pilot in your SLA addendum?

Regards,
Jenna Park
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Acme Cloud

Jenna / team —

Action plan + owners (draft) so we can lock milestones into the QBR deck:

- Infra benchmarks & candidate build (owner: Mateo Alvarez) — deliverable: benchmark report + candidate image by 2026-11-19.
- Routing integration (owner: Mateo + Eng routing pod) — integration test by 2026-11-22.
- Security focused review (owner: Aditya Rao) — security note confirming no PII cross-region routing by 2026-11-12.
- Procurement / PO execution (owner: Marissa Cole) — initial PO and invoice schedule by 2026-11-10. Attached: mutual_action_plan.xlsx and procurement-sheet-acme.csv (procurement asks).
- SLA exception: Vanessa to sign, Laura to include exception language in the QBR appendix.

Please reply if any owner cannot meet these dates. If all green I will update the QBR deck tomorrow and mark the mitigated-risk lane vs. a hard miss.

PRIYOM

Attachments referenced as stubs: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, procurement-sheet-acme.csv
